Though this appeal is listed for orders, with consent of both the learned counsels, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. The appellants-claimants, who are the legal representatives of deceased Govindaraju T.M., are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the compensation awarded under the judgment and award dated 17.08.2021 passed in MVC No.813/2019 by the Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Shiggaon, (for short, 'the Tribunal').
3.

Brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that the wife and children of the deceased Govindaraju T.M., filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation in respect of death of Govindaraju T.M. S/o.Pundalikappa in a road accident that took place on 20.05.2019 at about 11.00 a.m. It is averred that deceased had been to Shiralakoppa NC:
2023:KHC-D:7342-DB in TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-15/V-5822 as pillion rider and when they were proceeding near Shamanakatte village, a Hyundai car bearing Reg.No.KA-22/P-9701 driven by its driver in high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from back side and dashed the TVS XL, due to which the deceased Govindaraju fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government District Hospital, Anavatti, and while taking treatment he succumbed to injuries.
It is stated that the deceased was earning Rs.50,000/- per month by doing tailoring work and animal husbandry.

4. The respondents appeared before the Tribunal and filed objections denying the averments made in the claim petition, the mode of accident, age, income and avocation of the deceased, they have denied that the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased.
Respondent No.2 had averred that his vehicle was insured with respondent No.3 and the driver was having valid and effective driving license.
Respondent No.3-insurance NC: 2023:KHC-D:7342-DB company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy to the vehicle of respondent No.2.
Respondent No.3 has averred that driver of the vehicle in question was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of alleged accident.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence.
The claimant No.1, wife of the deceased, examined herself as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P24.
The respondents neither examined any witness nor got marked any documents.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.10,58,000/- with interest at 6%
per annum on the following heads:

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal & living expenses of the deceased, applied multiplier of 9.
The claimants, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.

7. Smt.Reshma Madiwalar, learned counsel for the appellants-claimants submits that the Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month, since the deceased was a Tailor by profession, 4 labourers were working under him, and he was also doing animal husbandry, and he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not granting any compensation towards loss of future prospects of the deceased.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in granting compensation towards other heads also, NC: 2023:KHC-D:7342-DB hence, she seeks for enhancement of compensation by allowing the appeal.

8. Per contra, Sri.Mallikarjun B.Madanalli, learned counsel for respondent No.1, Sri.Chandrashekar M.Hosamani, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Sri.Nagaraj C.Kalloori, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submit that the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month as the claimants have failed to produce any evidence before the Tribunal.

It is submitted that the Tribunal, taking into account the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court has awarded just and proper compensation which does not call for any enhancement in the present appeal and they seek to dismiss the appeal filed by the claimants.
9.
We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants-claimants, learned counsels for respondent NC: 2023:KHC-D:7342-DB Nos.1 to 3, perused the appeal papers and Tribunal records.

10. The points that arise for consideration in this appeal are:
i.
Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the income of deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month ?

11. The answer to the above point is answered in the negative for the following reasons.
a) There is no dispute that on 20.05.2019 the deceased Govindaraju was proceeding on the motorcycle and he has sustained grievous injuries in the road accident.
The r o a d a c c i d e n t h a s b e e n c a u s e d b y t h e o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-22-P-9701 and subsequently Govindaraju succumbed to those injuries.

It is also not in dispute that the legal heirs of deceased Govindaraju filed claim petition a n d o n c o n s i d e r i n g t h e e v i d e n c e , t h e T r i b u n a l h a s a s s e s s e d N C :
2023:KHC-D:7342-DB the income of deceased at Rs.10,000/-p.m.
It is not in dispute that the appellants have not produced any cogent and acceptable evidence before the Tribunal in support of the claim of income of the deceased.
The appellants have claimed that deceased was working as Tailor and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
However, no evidence has been placed before the Tribunal to substantiate the said claim.
In our considered view, the Tribunal committed error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month.
This Court and Lok-Adalaths normally rely on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the purpose of assessing the notional income while deciding the accident claims.
The accident is of the year 2019, as per the chart referred supra, the notional income of the deceased would be Rs.13,250/-.

We assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.13,250/- placing our reliance on the chart referred supra.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7342-DB b) The Tribunal has committed in error in awarding 15% compensation towards loss of future prospects.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others

In the instant case, the deceased was aged between 55-60 years as assessed by the Tribunal, hence, the appellants are entitled for addition of 10% towards the assessed income under the head of loss of future prospects instead of 15%.
c) The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation towards funeral expenses, loss of estate and loss of consortium, and the same does not call for any modification.
The Tribunal has applied 9 multiplier - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7342-DB and deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses and the same also does not call for any modification.

For the aforementioned reasons, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 17.08.2021 passed in MVC No.813/2019 by the S e n i o r C i v i l J u d g e & A d d l .

awarded by the Tribunal at the rate of 6% interest per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
iii) The respondent No.3-Insurance company shall deposit the entire compensation amount along with 6% interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
